URVARA.LIFE · A NATURAL CAPITAL COMPANY  ·  CNPI v1.2 · DRAFT FOR LANDSTACK01 / 100
00 · The question
For every rupee a company earns, how much pressure does it put on nature?
CNPI compares each company with peers in its own line of business, on four pressures the company reports.
A rank means
Among its peers, the company reported the lowest net pressure per rupee of revenue in FY2025-26 on climate, energy, water and pollution together, after counting the renewables, recycling and returned water it reports.
A rank does not mean
· a small footprint in absolute terms
· a biodiversity or land score: land appears as evidence
· an ESG rating, or a ranking across sectors
· that its supply chain or financed activity is covered
· that any company has done something wrong
Each comparison stays inside one peer group: cement makers meet cement makers, banks meet banks.

Nature cost, as a share of EBITDA
Each reported pressure × a published damage price (carbon at the India-borne share, water by scarcity, energy depletion, landfill, air health). Shown pressure by pressure, with % of revenue alongside. It stays out of the rank, and we do not add companies into a bill.

02 · Data quality: contradictions
26 companies report consuming more water than they withdraw, and 25 recovering more waste than they generate
We test each filing against itself: do the tables add up, and do the numbers agree?
26
consume more water than they withdraw
Two report zero withdrawal beside more than a million kL consumed. Above 10×, the value is held back; otherwise capped at withdrawal.
25
recover more waste than they generate
Stock drawn down is booked as this year’s recovery. Above 1.5×, held back. 114 of 465 claim at least 99% recovery.
91%
of all reported waste is one company’s overburden
Coal India reports 5.35 billion t generated and almost all of it recovered; GMDC, also a miner, reports 69 t.
441 / 465
data files do not state the Scope 2 basis
Without the basis, a low Scope 2 may reflect renewable contracts or an error.
42
imply a grid factor outside 0.5–1.0 t/MWh
Scope 2 divided by purchased non-renewable electricity: from 0.0007 to 141 t/MWh, where the grid is about 0.71.
10
emitters above 1 Mt Scope 1 report no air tonnage
Including NLC India (31.6 Mt) and Coal India (28.2 Mt). 111 companies report air as concentrations, with no mass.
Counts across all 500 from the current build; grid-factor and air tests from the analyst review of the same files (insights/pressures).
We list each case so that the company can confirm or correct its figure.

03 · Method: principles
Six rules decide what enters a rank
01
Company data only
Ranks use what companies report. We add no estimates or models, and a blank stays blank.
02
Every number traceable
Each value carries its link, page or filing field, and the exact quote when taken from a report.
03
Like with like
A company meets peers in its own business, and a group needs 8 with complete data.
04
Simple, open maths
Anyone can reproduce every score; the dataset recomputes all 500 with spreadsheet formulas.
05
Doubtful values held back
We hold back a value that looks wrong until the company confirms it, even when it is printed.
06
Good practice counts in full
Renewables, recycling and returned water reduce the pressure they act on, with no cap. Tree planting cannot cancel emissions.
Each ranked number traces to the company’s own disclosure.

03 · Method: which greenhouse gases
CNPI scores Scope 1 and Scope 2; 126 of 465 filings give a usable Scope 3
The GHG Protocol splits a company’s emissions into three scopes. CNPI scores the two that each BRSR must report and the company controls.
Scored
Scope 1
Direct emissions from the company’s own sites: fuel burnt in boilers, kilns, furnaces and vehicles, gases released by processes such as clinker-making, and refrigerant leaks.
Scored
Scope 2
Emissions from generating the electricity the company buys. We take it as reported: 441 of 465 data files do not say whether it uses the grid average or contracts bought. We accept a zero where the filing shows at least 90% renewable supply.
Not scored
Scope 3
Everything upstream and downstream: suppliers, transport, use of products, and for banks, what they finance. 126 of 465 data files give a positive figure in a clear unit, on different boundaries.
Scope 1 + Scope 2, in tonnes of CO2-equivalent, for FY2025-26.

03 · Method: the formula
ACC scores 86.1 and ranks #1 of 10 cement makers; you can check it by hand
Intensity = net pressure ÷ revenue. Line up the peers from lowest to highest, score 100 to 0, average the pressures, rank. ACC revenue ₹25,766 crore.
score = 100 × (n − position) ÷ (n − 1)   position 1 = lowest intensity; ties share the average position; final score = mean of the scored pressures

03 · Method: held-back values
We hold back 29 printed values until the company confirms them
The 29 values on the four pressures come from 24 companies; we show 11 more unscored where pollution is not scored. All stay in the dataset with a flag.
16
Extreme values
Gross figure more than 300× above or below the peer median per ₹ crore. Typical cause: a unit slip or a head-office-only boundary.
8
Inconsistent tables
Water consumed more than 10× water withdrawn, or waste recovered more than 1.5× waste generated.
2
Impossible Scope 2
A Scope 2 figure implying an electricity bill larger than the company’s whole revenue (₹6/kWh, 0.71 t/MWh).
New in v1.2
3
Scope 2 above energy
Scope 2 implying more grid electricity than 1.5× the company’s total reported energy: Coal India, Canara HSBC Life Insu…, Ingersoll-Rand (India).
New in v1.2
7
Zero Scope 2 accepted
We accept a zero Scope 2 where the filing shows at least 90% renewable energy or electricity. 7 of these are ranked.
New in v1.2
30
Assumed discharge
Consumption printed at a fixed 20% of withdrawal assumes 80% returned; we credit no offset and score water on withdrawal (24 ranked).
13
Zeros to confirm
Any other zero total, or a zero Scope 1 or Scope 2 alone. For an operating company, a zero tends to mean ‘not measured’.
A company with a held-back value on a scored pressure enters the rank once it resolves the value.

03 · Method: where pollution is not scored
In four groups companies count their biggest waste stream in different ways, so pollution stays out of their rank
Scoring waste there would reward whoever left the biggest stream out. The rank uses climate, energy and water; the slides show the waste figures unscored.
Power
Fly ash
NTPC reports 57 thousand tonnes of waste in its BRSR table, far below a coal fleet’s ash; Reliance Power reports 106.7 million and Adani Power 16.8 million tonnes.
Non-ferrous metals & mining
Overburden & tailings
Coal India counts 5.35 billion tonnes of overburden, almost all as recovered. Hindustan Zinc reports 20 million tonnes; GMDC, a lignite miner, 69 tonnes.
Construction & engineering
Construction debris
Larsen & Toubro reports about 596 thousand tonnes; IRCON (10 t), RVNL (33 t) and NBCC (24 t) report almost none.
Real estate
Demolition & site debris
Godrej Properties reports 2.9 million tonnes and Brigade 2.0 million, almost all recovered; Anant Raj reports 0.74 t and Phoenix Mills 598 t.
In the other 20 groups a company needs all four pressures, so leaving one out cannot help it.

03 · Method: land and biodiversity
13 of 500 companies print a company-wide land total, too few to score land
BRSR has no field for land area. It asks how many plants a company has, and whether any sit in or near an ecologically sensitive area, in free text.
13
companies print a company-wide land total, out of 500
6 developers give a land bank, 7 a figure for a different boundary, 51 an older or partial one. Owned, leased and mining-lease areas are different quantities.
Proposed method · to decide once the data exist
site area × (1 − MSA) × proximity weight
MSA, mean species abundance (GLOBIO): the share of original species abundance that survives under a land use.
Proximity weight rises for sites in or near protected areas (WDPA) and Key Biodiversity Areas.
It needs site polygons or coordinates: today 10 of 326 sites found have them.

What the filings show
Scope 2 follows the grid average: for 286 of 433 companies, Scope 2 ÷ purchased electricity equals the CEA FY2024-25 grid factor (0.71 t/MWh), though 441 of 465 data files do not state the method.
42 companies imply a grid factor outside 0.5–1.0 t/MWh (Nestlé India 141, Torrent Power 26.5); we hold back three whose Scope 2 exceeds 1.5× their total energy.
Scope 2 is 3% of Scope 1+2 in cement but 94% in banks: in services, the climate score is an electricity score.
Captive power moves emissions from Scope 2 to Scope 1 while the electricity may still be reported as consumed.
The number can support
Ranking companies within a peer group on operational Scope 1+2 per rupee.
It cannot support
Adding companies into national totals (power’s Scope 1 reappears as others’ Scope 2); renewable claims without a market-based figure; value-chain or financed emissions.
Findings: CNPI analyst review of the same files (insights/pressures), checked against the current build.
Light green = financial groupsClimate decides most ranks in heavy industry; in services it is an electricity score.

What the filings show
Consumption is not computed by one rule: 189 of 468 report consumption equal to withdrawal, many while also reporting discharge; 66 of 454 fail the water balance by more than 10%.
30 companies print consumption at a fixed 20% of withdrawal, an assumed 80% discharge. We credit no offset and score them on withdrawal.
Seawater and once-through cooling are mixed with freshwater: 83% of Adani Power’s 966 million kL is seawater; Tata Power withdraws 3.70 billion kL and consumes 266 million.
Held back: consumption above 10× withdrawal (BEML, Privi Speciality, and Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Finserv against a zero withdrawal).
The number can support
Within-group comparison of water taken and not returned, per rupee.
It cannot support
Any statement about scarcity or basin stress: there are no facility coordinates, and freshwater is not separated from seawater.

What the filings show
140 companies give at least one site area (252 sites), and 10 sites carry printed coordinates, too few to screen overlap with protected areas.
Of 87 sensitive-area answers found (59 companies), most are denials or blank placeholders; 13 companies state that a site is in, near or surrounded by a sensitive area.
Owned, leased, mining-lease and land-bank areas are different quantities: Oil India’s 482,884 ha is the area of 25 petroleum mining leases, not land occupied.
IIM Bangalore: 80.0% of the top 1,000 report operations in or around sensitive areas, yet 76.0% have no credible biodiversity disclosure.
The evidence can support
That a company holds land, and where some of its sites are.
It cannot support
Any rank, any biodiversity-impact estimate, or a peer comparison.
Land is the missing disclosure: without it there is no biodiversity rank.

01

02
LT Foods (91.8% renewable) climbs from 16th on gross figures to 6th net, Nestlé India from 24th to 16th and United Spirits from 7th to 1st. Allied Blenders recovers none of its waste and drops from 11th to 20th; Cupid (₹358 crore revenue, no waste recovery) drops from 5th to 12th.
03
Hindustan Unilever (4th), United Breweries (13th) and Cupid (12th) rank on a zero Scope 2, which CNPI accepts because they report 96–100% renewable electricity. HUL has the group's lowest climate intensity (0.11 tCO2e per ₹ crore), which widens the climate spread to 954 times (E.I.D. Parry 104.4).
04
ITC emits 27.0% of the group's Scope 1+2 and ranks 23rd. It returns 63.5% of the water it withdraws, the group's highest share. Radico Khaitan recovers none of its waste and holds 46.8% of the group's unrecovered waste; United Breweries holds 18.1%.
05
Water spans 832 times (P&G Hygiene 1.85, E.I.D. Parry 1,538 kL per ₹ crore). E.I.D. Parry, a sugar company, ranks last. 22 of 27 ranked companies report air in tonnes.

01

02
Six banks reported water use as a flat 20% of withdrawal, assuming 80% goes out as discharge. CNPI scores them on withdrawal: HDFC Bank (11th), Federal (6th), IndusInd (18th), Karur Vysya (22nd), RBL (4th) and Punjab & Sind (23rd).
03
Water and climate scores show no link (rank correlation −0.07). Bandhan ranks first on climate and energy, last on water (32.9 kL per ₹ crore), and 8th overall. Axis Bank has the lowest water intensity (1.33 kL) and ranks 3rd.
04
SBI emits 24.3% of the group's Scope 1+2 and ranks 10th. ICICI (84.8) is the highest-ranked like-for-like bank, ahead of Yes Bank (83.8) and Axis (74.0). Kotak returns 76% of its water and gains the most from offsets, climbing from 23rd on gross figures to 16th net.
05
Revenue-based and profit-based ranks correlate at 0.52, the second-lowest of any group. For banks, the choice of yardstick moves the result.
Operational footprint: offices, branches and data centres. Lending, investing and insuring sit outside it. Not ranked here: 2 (Central Bank of India, Jammu and Kashmir Bank); reasons on the next slide and in the dataset.

06 · What a real corporate nature index needs · 1 of 3
Companies report climate, energy and waste; they omit the basis behind each figure
Climate (GHG)
Medium gap
A real index needs
Scope 1 by source (combustion/process/fugitive); Scope 2 location- AND market-based with grid factor version; GHG consolidation approach matched to revenue boundary; Scope 3 by category (tCO2e; company, site for large emitters)
BRSR today
EI 7: Scope 1 and Scope 2 totals + intensities; LI 2: Scope 3 (voluntary). No method, factor, boundary or source split
What the 500 show
S1+S2 473/500 (13 with an unconfirmed zero component); Scope 2 method stated 16/465; implied factor = CEA FY25 0.71 for 286/433; 42 fail Scope 2 vs electricity test (3 now held back by the 1.5x-energy rule, 34 still ranked); Scope 3 positive in a clear unit 126/465
The one ask
State the Scope 2 method and grid-factor version (report location-based and market-based separately) and the GHG consolidation boundary
Standards: IFRS S2 (location-based Scope 2 required); ESRS E1-6; GRI 305-1..3 (GRI 102 from 2027)
Energy
Medium gap
A real index needs
Fuel by type (GJ); grid electricity purchased (MWh); captive generation with the fuel already counted; renewable split on-site / contracted / certificate; biomass with source (company, site)
BRSR today
EI 1: electricity, fuel, other; renewable vs non-renewable; intensities. No captive-vs-grid or fuel-type split
What the 500 show
473/500; electricity/fuel split 461/465; 10 XBRL totals wrong by 10^3-10^12 vs PDF; 38 values for 13 companies hand-corrected; captive generation identifiable in 0
The one ask
Report grid-purchased and self-generated electricity on separate lines, naming the fuel already counted for self-generation
Standards: GRI 302 (GRI 103 from 2027); ESRS E1-5; BRSR Core energy footprint
Waste incl. hazardous
Medium gap
A real index needs
Generated by hazard class and stream; named mineral streams (fly ash, overburden, tailings, slag, C&D); diverted vs disposed by hazard class; stock recovery separate (t)
BRSR today
EI 9: 8 categories incl. other hazardous; recovered (3 routes); disposed (3 routes); no stock line, no mineral-stream lines
What the 500 show
472/500; hazardous category filled 57/57, positive in 43/57 (57-subset); 21 recover more than generated; 72/449 do not balance; pollution unscored in 4 groups (Power, Non-ferrous & mining, Construction & engineering, Real estate; e.g. Coal India 5.35 bn t vs GMDC 69 t)
The one ask
Report fly ash, overburden, tailings and slag as named lines, and recovery from stock separately from current-year arisings
Standards: GRI 306-3/4/5; ESRS E5-5; TNFD C2.2, C2.3; BRSR Core circularity
URVARA.LIFE · A NATURAL CAPITAL COMPANY  ·  CNPI v1.2 · DRAFT FOR LANDSTACK94 / 100
06 · What a real corporate nature index needs · 2 of 3
Water and air need location, pollutant loads and mass in tonnes
Water quantity
Medium gap
A real index needs
Withdrawal by source, discharge by destination, consumption = withdrawal - discharge (+/- storage), freshwater vs other (m3; site)
BRSR today
EI 3: withdrawal by 5 sources + consumption; EI 4: discharge by destination and treatment (company only)
What the 500 show
Consumption 473/500; consumption = withdrawal in 189/468 (49 of them with positive discharge); water balance fails >10% in 66/454; discharge > withdrawal in 2; 30 report consumption at a fixed 20% of withdrawal (scored on withdrawal in the final build)
The one ask
Compute consumption as withdrawal minus discharge (plus/minus storage) and report seawater separately from freshwater in the totals
Standards: GRI 303-3/4/5; ESRS E3-4; TNFD C3.0
Water source location and stress
High gap
A real index needs
Facility coordinates or district/basin; withdrawal and consumption per facility; stress class with named dataset (WRI Aqueduct or CGWB block); groundwater share
BRSR today
LI 1 (voluntary): per-facility table for 'areas of water stress' with area name only; no coordinates, no definition of stress
What the 500 show
Water-stress values 20/57 (57-subset); groundwater used by 36/57; facility coordinates 0 in BRSR; district known for 280/326 Hermes sites
The one ask
Make the water-stress facility table mandatory, with district and coordinates per facility and the stress dataset named
Standards: TNFD C3.0; GRI 303-3-b, 303-5-b; ESRS E3-4; SBTN freshwater (basin)
Wastewater and water/soil pollution
High gap
A real index needs
Discharge by receiving body; pollutant loads (BOD, COD, N, P, metals) in t/yr; treatment level; pollutants released to soil (site)
BRSR today
EI 4: discharge volume by destination and treatment level; no loads, no soil releases
What the 500 show
Discharge total 463/465 parsed; destination/treatment tags present 57/57 (57-subset); pollutant loads 0 (not asked); not used in CNPI
The one ask
Add annual pollutant loads (t/yr of COD, BOD, total N, total P) per discharge point, as already monitored under SPCB consents
Standards: TNFD C2.1, C2.0; GRI 303-4; ESRS E2-4
Air pollutants (non-GHG)
High gap
A real index needs
NOx, SOx, PM2.5/PM10, NMVOC, NH3 as annual mass (t/yr); sources covered; CEMS vs calculated (site)
BRSR today
EI 6: NOx, SOx, PM, POP, VOC, HAP, others with 'please specify unit'; no mass rule, no PM size, no NH3
What the 500 show
NOx+SOx+PM in tonnes 245/500 (178 ranked); 111 excluded for non-mass units; 10 firms with >1 Mt Scope 1 report no air tonnage
The one ask
Require NOx, SOx and PM in tonnes per year (annual mass), not concentrations
Standards: TNFD C2.4; GRI 305-7; ESRS E2-4

06 · What a real corporate nature index needs · 3 of 3
Land, biodiversity and the value chain are the three critical gaps
Land use and land-use change
Critical gap
A real index needs
Area owned/leased/mining lease; disturbed area; rehabilitated/restored area; conversion in the year by ecosystem type (ha); polygons for sites >=10 ha
BRSR today
Section A: number of plants/offices only; EI 12: EIA list; no area field of any kind
What the 500 show
Company-wide land total 13/500, plus 6 real-estate land banks and 7 figures for a partial boundary (77 with any figure); site area for 140 companies (252 sites); coordinates for 10 sites; disturbed or converted area 0 as standard fields
The one ask
Add a land table: hectares owned, leased and under mining lease, plus area disturbed and restored in the year, on the BRSR boundary
Standards: TNFD C1.0, C1.1; GRI 101-5; SBTN Land (no conversion, footprint, landscape)
Biodiversity: sensitive sites and state of nature
Critical gap
A real index needs
Site coordinates/polygon; overlap or distance to PAs, KBAs, Ramsar, ESZ, tiger reserves (named dataset); natural ecosystem extent and condition change; threatened species; restoration (site)
BRSR today
EI 11: free-text table of operations in/around ecologically sensitive areas (no coordinates, distance or area); LI 3 (voluntary): impact narrative
What the 500 show
Hermes: 87 sensitive-area answers from 59 companies, mostly denials or blank; 13 companies state a site is in or near a sensitive area; coordinates for 10 of 326 sites
The one ask
Give coordinates (polygon for sites of 10 ha or more) and area for every operating site, so overlap with protected areas and KBAs can be screened independently
Standards: TNFD C5.0-C5.2; GRI 101-5, 101-7 (formerly 304-1, 304-4); ESRS E4-5; SBTN Step 1
Value chain: commodities and Scope 3
Critical gap
A real index needs
Tonnes of high-impact natural commodities by type and origin; share certified; Scope 3 by category
BRSR today
LI 2: Scope 3 (voluntary); Principle 2: % of inputs sourced sustainably (no tonnes, no origin)
What the 500 show
Scope 3 positive in a clear unit 126/465; commodity tonnes by origin 0 (not asked)
The one ask
Report tonnes of high-impact natural commodities sourced by type and origin state/country, with share certified (TNFD C3.1)
Standards: TNFD C3.1; IFRS S2; ESRS E1-6; SBTN Step 1

07 · What would make CNPI stronger
Five disclosures would let CNPI score land and biodiversity
Ask 01
Land
Hectares owned, leased and under mining lease, plus area disturbed and restored in the year, on the BRSR boundary.
Ask 02
Sites
Coordinates (a polygon for sites of 10 ha or more) for every operating site, so overlap with protected areas can be screened.
Ask 03
Scope 2
State the basis: location-based and market-based, with the grid-factor version, and the GHG boundary.
Ask 04
Air
NOx, SOx and PM as annual mass in tonnes, in place of stack concentrations.
Ask 05
Water & waste
Measured discharge, seawater apart from freshwater; fly ash, overburden, tailings and slag as named lines, stock recovery apart.
Companies can correct any value with a page reference to their own published report.
